rationale: The round-0 candidate built and ran cleanly with no ICE, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up while respecting the program's profile: it is a floating-point compute benchmark (oourafft FFT kernels cftmdl/cft1st/cdft plus whetstone/fbench-style loops) where runtime overhead is the binding constraint. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since arithmetic substitution is cheap, correctness-safe, and especially effective against the dense float/int arithmetic dominating these kernels. IBR and ICALL are raised next because branch and call indirection break the control-flow graph and cross-referencing that reversers rely on, at modest constant-factor cost. IGV is kept strong to obscure the FFT twiddle/index constants and global state. BCF is moderately weighted but with elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost so the scheduler confines bogus control flow to the smaller functions (bitrv2, main) rather than the hot 12KB cftmdl body. FLA is retained only with low SecurityGain and the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost, since flattening inner float loops would crush benchmark runtime for limited gain; SPLIT stays lightweight to improve resilience of the other passes by shrinking basic blocks. All CorrectnessRisk values stay low since round 0 showed full correctness, and the float-heavy code tolerates these transforms well.
